```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(symcompR)
x <- Symbol("x"); y <- Symbol("y")
n <- Symbol("n", integer = TRUE)
```

symcompR has both assumptions systems of SymPy: facts attached to symbols
(the "old" assumptions of `sympy.core.assumptions`) and predicates queried
with `ask()` (`sympy.assumptions`).

## Assumptions on symbols

`Symbol()` accepts assumptions as arguments. The `is_*()` queries return
`TRUE`, `FALSE`, or `NA` when the answer is not known, and `ask_fact()`
queries any fact by name.

```{r}
p <- Symbol("p", positive = TRUE)
r <- Symbol("r", real = TRUE)
is_negative(1 - sqrt(S(2)))
is_nonnegative(p)
is_nonpositive(-p)
is_nonzero(p)
is_zero(p - p)
is_finite(r)
is_infinite(oo * sym_I)
is_complex(r)
is_imaginary(sym_I * r)
is_imaginary(2 * sym_I)
is_rational(Rational(1, 3))
is_irrational(sqrt(S(2)))
is_algebraic(sqrt(S(2)))
is_transcendental(sym_pi)
is_odd(2 * n + 1)
is_prime_expr(S(7))
is_commutative(x)
ask_fact(p + 1, "positive")
ask_fact(x, "positive")
```

`check_assumptions()` tests an expression against a set of assumptions,
`failing_assumptions()` lists the ones that fail, and `assumptions()` lists
the known assumptions of an expression.

```{r}
check_assumptions(S(-2), integer = TRUE, positive = TRUE)
check_assumptions(p + 1, positive = TRUE)
failing_assumptions(S(-2), integer = TRUE, positive = TRUE)
assumptions(x)
```

## Predicates with `ask()` and `refine()`

The second assumptions system keeps facts separate from symbols: predicates such
as `Q$positive(x)` are queried with `ask()`, which returns `TRUE`, `FALSE`,
or `NA` (unknown). Further arguments are assumptions to use.

```{r}
ask(Q$positive(x))
ask(Q$positive(x^2 + 1), Q$real(x))
ask(Q$integer(x + y), Q$integer(x), Q$integer(y))
ask(Q$positive(x * y), Q$negative(x), Q$negative(y))
ask(Q$even(2 * n))
ask(Q$prime(7))
ask(Q$rational(sqrt(S(2))))
```

`refine()` simplifies an expression using assumptions.

```{r}
refine(sqrt(x^2), Q$positive(x))
refine(Abs(x), Q$negative(x))
refine((-1)^n, Q$even(n))
```

`assuming()` evaluates an expression with assumptions added to the global
context, and removes them afterwards.

```{r}
assuming(Q$positive(x), refine(sqrt(x^2)))
assuming(Q$positive(x), ask(Q$real(x)))
ask(Q$real(x))
```


An `AssumptionsContext` is a set of facts. `global_assumptions` is the
context that `ask()` always consults; `assuming()` adds to it temporarily.

```{r}
ctx <- AssumptionsContext(Q$positive(x))
ctx
global_assumptions
```

## Custom predicates and other solvers

`Predicate()` creates a new predicate and `AppliedPredicate()` applies one
to arguments. A predicate created with `dispatch = TRUE` answers through
handlers added by `register_predicate()` for given expression types.

```{r}
P <- Predicate("P")
P(x)
ask(P(x), P(x) & Q$positive(x))
AppliedPredicate(Q$integer, x)
K <- Predicate("my_key", dispatch = TRUE)
register_predicate(K, "Symbol", function(expr, assumptions) TRUE)
ask(K(x))
ask(K(x + 1))
```

`satask()` decides a query with a SAT solver, and `lra_satask()` with
linear real arithmetic, which also handles inequalities between real
symbols:

```{r}
y <- Symbol("y")
satask(Q$zero(Abs(y)), Q$zero(y))
satask(Q$positive(x * y), Q$positive(x) & Q$positive(y))
xr <- Symbol("xr", real = TRUE)
lra_satask(Q$gt(xr, 0), Q$gt(xr, 1))
lra_satask(Q$lt(xr, 0), Q$gt(xr, 1))
lra_satask(Q$eq(xr, 1), !Q$ne(xr, 0))
```

`AssumptionsWrapper()` reads the assumption properties of an expression
under extra assumptions, and `is_extended_real()` and
`is_extended_nonnegative()` are shortcuts for two of them.

```{r}
AssumptionsWrapper(y)$is_positive
AssumptionsWrapper(y, Q$positive(y))$is_positive
is_extended_real(y, Q$extended_real(y))
is_extended_nonnegative(y, Q$positive(y))
is_extended_nonnegative(y)
```
